narrative:
Your application was denied because the model assessed you as a bad credit risk, with a predicted probability of default of 47%. That means the model found nearly a one-in-two chance you would have trouble repaying the loan — a risk level the bank considers too high to accept.

Three main factors drove this decision. The most influential was the purpose of the loan: you requested financing for a new car. Applicants asking for new-car loans are more likely to default than those borrowing for other purposes, so this pushed your risk upward. Next, the amount you asked for — 6,260 DM — was about twice the average approved loan amount. While a larger loan can sometimes signal confidence, in your case it contributed to the model’s caution, actually pulling slightly toward a good-risk assessment because you requested a manageable sum relative to your income. Still, the final weight of this factor was not enough to offset other concerns. The third major factor was your checking account status: you have a balance between 0 and 200 DM. This indicates limited financial buffer and was a strong signal pushing toward bad credit, as most approved applicants have no balance or more substantial funds.

To improve your chances in the future, consider strengthening your financial profile. Build up a larger savings cushion, maintain a higher checking account balance, and perhaps wait until you can request a smaller loan or choose a purpose associated with lower risk, such as furniture or equipment. Reapplying after these changes may lead to a different outcome.
